Not sure why their `insertHTML` function inserts it twice, one in `<head>` and one in `<body>`.
Also from the docs they say it should be in `layout.js` but seems like it works in a `page.js` file ?
probably don't want to keep this?
In theory doesn't even need to be linked to next, more server components
this is a promise, could we add it to the chain or does it not make sense?
is it required to be a client component? I guess so as we have client interactivity as well
what ensures that at this point _all_ widgets have been mounted and not just the first one?
something on the TriggerSearch "widget" maybe could be used
in the future we'll need to rename promiseRef, as it's not too clear what it's goal is

Some of it does, as injecting `initialResults` uses a Next.js-specific API.
Most of the changes will be directly in `react-instantsearch`, with packaged tiny wrappers for frameworks that just inject initial results with their framework's API.
Yeah, leftovers from when I tested SEO 😅
Or they could indeed just pass their own `insertHTML` function, but I think it's nice to just have to replace `<InstantSearch>` with no prop change
Whichever component that has `<InstantSearch>` at its root yes, but they're free to have a server component in `page.js` which also contains their search component
It's appended after `<InstantSearch>`'s children so they should all have been added at this point, might not with portals or something though
Do you get a clear error if it's accidentally a server component? if not we should give some warnign/error

They would as `<InstantSearch>` calls hooks, but probably not the clearest.
We'll have to test a lot of scenarios yes 😅
The stack trace might not be clear enough, but the message explicitly say "Please add 'use client'" and the stack trace finishes at the `page.tsx` (or whatever page in which they add InstantSearch).

Tried adding `'use client'` in `react-instantsearch/index.ts` but it throws an error that you can't do `export *` in a client boundary.
Anyway I've seen that Apollo and other libs have users place `'use client'` themselves, and I think it's probably better that they explicitly add their boundaries themselves rather than it being hidden in the library which can be confusing.
do we not need to wait on the stream to end or something? seems like in react 18 it's a single buffer but I don't think that's guaranteed
we can't get rid of the fallback without a breaking change, as older react versions (that don't use server side rendering for example) don't have use
